name: build-jail-preset
note: MECHANISM PIN, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING: without ambient_env NUB_SANDBOX_MECHANISM=landlock this fixture measured a DIFFERENT BACKEND than the one it gates, and every expectation below was wrong for what it actually drove. `policy.build_jail` is set only by `compile_build_jail` (preset.rs), which the shipped install path uses; the bare "build-jail" preset string resolves through `compile_scope`, leaves the flag false, and `linux_landlock.rs` returns NotABuildJail -> Bubblewrap, where the project-root ListOnly node grant renders as a full --ro-bind subtree. MEASURED on kernel 6.17, same binary and fixture, only this variable differing: under bwrap `source.txt`, `.env`, `nested/.env`, `.npmrc` and `.git/hooks/pre-commit` were ALL readable, against DENIED on Landlock -- 5 of the 8 cases, though CI reported one because assert_eq! aborts at the first. The controls (node_modules, package.json) fire in both arms, so neither backend was a vacuous jail. The default-on install path was never affected: it reaches Landlock via compile_build_jail. The build-jail preset compiled standalone: the DEPENDENCY TREE reads (not writes), the consumer's own source does NOT, its secret + .env floors hold, env is strip-all, and egress is curated to the $downloads set (the connect case targets an IP literal, which is outside it). A measured read-ladder study narrowed the read set to <project>/node_modules + <project>/package.json, so `proj:source.txt` asserts DENIED where it once asserted readable — that flip is the tightening. The node_modules read is the positive control: without it a denial here would equally describe a jail that never started. `package.json` is granted but deliberately NOT probed, because the harness materializes every read target and would overwrite the workspace manifest the Linux preflight consumes. The .env cases now pass because the consumer's tree is outside the read set entirely rather than because the floor masked them; they are kept as regression cover for the day a project read widens again. The per-package WRITE grant, the provisioned-interpreter read grant, and the scrubbed lifecycle env are supplied per spawn by the lifecycle interposition (compile_build_jail), not this static preset. The .env cases assert `read-content` (no bytes disclosed) rather than `read` (open refused), because the backends deny a builtin-floor dotenv file in two different shapes and only one fails at open: macOS Seatbelt refuses the path, while Linux mount-masks it present-but-empty so a dotenv reader gets no secret instead of a hard error. Non-disclosure is the property that holds on both, and the relaxed negative control still reads the file's bytes, so the assertion cannot go hollow.
